akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً﴾: their singular is الفَوْج (a troop).

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿َفسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾: He means "let your glorification be with praise" (يَكُونُ تسبيحُك بالحَمْد), because "التَسْبيح" (glorification) is remembrance (dhikr); so He said: "let your remembrance be with praise for what I have given you, the conquest of Mecca and other things". And a man says "قَضَيْتُ سُبْحتي من الذكر" ("I have completed my subḥa of remembrance").

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial (ẓarfiyya), conditional, non-jussive. ﴿جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْفَتْحُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَرَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿يَدْخُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَفْواجاً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ﴾ an imperative verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانَ﴾ kāna and its latent noun. ﴿تَوَّاباً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. The nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

farraa:1-2.t:
His words: ﴿إِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْفَتْحُ﴾.
Meaning the conquest of Mecca. ﴿وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً﴾.
He says: and you saw the tribes, a whole tribe accepting Islam at once; before that, a man would accept Islam only after another man. [Translator's note: the source has «وقيل ذلك», apparently for «وقبل ذلك» (before that); translated by the latter.]

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾.
He says: then pray. And they mentioned that he ﷺ said when this surah was revealed: My own death has been announced to me.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Naṣr
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ والفَتْحُ﴾ ("when the help of Allah and the victory come"): it was said that the victory, as has come in the exegesis, [means] that the Prophet's ﷺ own death was announced to him in this sūra: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, let him know that when the conquest of Mecca came and people entered Islam in crowds, his appointed term ﷺ had drawn near. He used to say that: «”إنَّهُ قَدْ نُعِيَتْ إلَيَّ نَفْسِي في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ“» ("my death has been announced to me in this sūra"). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded him to increase glorification and seeking forgiveness, so that He might seal for him, at the end of his life, with an increase in righteous deeds, by following what He commanded him.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَرَأيْتَ النّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ في دِينِ اللَّهِ أفْواجًا﴾ ("and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds"): the meaning of ﴿أفْواجًا﴾ is large groups; that is, after they used to enter one by one and two by two, the tribe came to enter Islam in its entirety.
